To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) IN‐OT does not reduce anxiety in a public speaking paradigm (2) IN‐OT increases the perception of the trustworthiness and attractiveness of faces in women but not in men, (3) IN‐OT has no effects on trust, cooperation, and generosity, and (4) IN‐OT reduces the perception of the attractiveness of faces in men.

IN‐OT has no effect on the ability of subjects to detect emotional expressions in the eyes of others (study 1), does not affect the ability of subjects with borderline personality disorder to recognize emotions in the eyes of their romantic partners, nor does it affect their ability to regulate their own emotions (study 2), does not affect empathy in healthy subjects (study 3), does not affect trust in healthy subjects (studies 4 and 6) and does not affect trust or trustworth
IN‐OT does not increase social approach and does not reduce social avoidance in humans.

the effects of IN–OT are more complex and less robust than is generally thought.
there is no publication bias in our IN‐OT research but that we have been too optimistic and too quick in publishing our results.
IN‐OT has no effects on the social and emotional behaviour of humans, at least as measured by the paradigms we used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
OT does not have a robust effect on human behaviour and, in particular, does not seem to have the effects that were expected.
IN‐OT does not seem to have any consistent effect on human social behaviour, at least in the doses that have been used so far.
, in our hands, IN‐OT does not seem to be a panacea for the treatment of social deficits in humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of INOT in humans are much less robust than what the current literature suggests.
IN‐OT research is still a young field, and that the current literature should be considered with caution.
the IN‐OT field should move towards more transparency, more replication and a better understanding of the pharmacological properties and the mechanisms of action of OT.
